h1: The 8 Best Lockable Laptop Charging Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lockable Charging Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight lockable laptop charging carts for schools and offices, from 12 to 30 devices, with picks by capacity and lock design.
summary: The POCHAR 30 Unit cart is our best overall pick for large classrooms, with front and rear key locks and two keys for each. The Pearington 20 Device cart is the best mid-size choice thanks to its locking casters, and the Learniture 12-Device station is the budget pick for small groups. Capacities range from 12 to 30 devices.
intro: Most buyers choose a charging cart by device count and only later discover that a lock on one door does not secure the back. A cart with a locked front and an open rear panel protects nothing, so the lock layout matters as much as the capacity.

We reviewed eight lockable carts on paper, comparing capacity, lock placement, mobility features and price bucket. We ranked them for classroom and shared-office use, and every one of them lists a lock.

products.name: POCHAR 30 Unit Device Charging Station for Chromebook, iPad, 14'' Laptop
products.verdict: Large capacity with locks on both the front and rear.
products.description:
This POCHAR cart holds 30 devices, including Chromebooks, iPads and 14 inch laptops. It has front and rear key locks, with two keys supplied for each.

It wins because the rear lock closes the gap many carts leave open, and 30 slots cover a full classroom. The tradeoff is a bigger frame and a price in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Choose it for a full class set. Skip it if you only manage a handful of devices.
products.skipIf: You manage only a few devices.

products.name: Pearington 20 Device Mobile Charging and Storage Cart for iPads, Chromebooks
products.verdict: Locking doors plus two locking casters for a cart that stays put.
products.description:
The Pearington holds 20 devices behind door locks and rolls on casters, two of which lock. It suits iPads and Chromebooks and sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Second place reflects that locking casters keep it from rolling while you load or unload, a detail the other 20 device carts do not list. It holds fewer devices than the POCHAR 30.

Pick it for mid-size classes that share a cart between rooms. Skip it for sets larger than 20.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: A 20 device cart that arrives assembled with front and back locks.
products.description:
The Meteteel holds 20 devices, ships fully assembled and has front and back door locks, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Third spot comes down to the fact that it matches the Pearington on capacity but does not list locking casters. The assembled delivery saves setup time.

It suits schools without time for assembly. Skip it if you want locking wheels.
products.idealFor: Schools that want it ready to roll.

products.name: POCHAR 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for iPads Chromebooks, Tablet Charging Station
products.verdict: Locking doors plus a chain hook anchor point.
products.description:
This POCHAR holds 20 devices behind locking doors and adds a chain hook anchor point, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Fourth position follows from the fact that the anchor point helps tether the cart to a fixed object, which others here do not list, while the Pearington adds locking casters instead.

Choose it where theft is the concern. Skip it if you want a front and rear lock layout.
products.idealFor: Spaces where theft is a concern.
products.skipIf: You want front and rear locks.

products.name: Pearington 30 Device Mobile Charging/Storage Cart for iPads, Tablets, Laptop
products.verdict: A 30 device cart with secure lockable storage.
products.description:
The Pearington 30 holds 30 devices in secure lockable storage, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Fifth place is explained by the fact that its lock details are less specific than the POCHAR 30, which names front and rear key locks and two keys each.

It suits large sets in one room. Skip it if you want documented rear locks.
products.idealFor: Large device sets in one building.
products.skipIf: You want a stated rear lock.

products.name: VEVOR 16 Device Charging Station with Lock & Key, Mobile Charging Cart
products.verdict: A 16 device cart that adds surge protection to the lock.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 16 devices, comes with a lock and key and lists surge protection, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Sixth place is down to the fact that it has fewer slots than the 20 device carts in the same price bucket. The surge protection is a distinct benefit.

Choose it for a smaller set where power safety matters. Skip it if you need 20 or more slots.
cons: Same price tier as larger carts
products.idealFor: Small sets where power safety matters.

products.name: AQNIEGEP 16-Device Charging Station, Black
products.verdict: A 16 device security cabinet design in black.
products.description:
The AQNIEGEP holds 16 devices in a security cabinet design, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Seventh place follows from the fact that the listing gives less detail on locks than the VEVOR, which names a lock and key.

It suits shared spaces that want an enclosed look. Skip it if you want surge protection spelled out.
products.idealFor: Shared spaces wanting an enclosed look.

products.name: Learniture Structure Series 12-Device Charging Station for Laptops and Tablets
products.verdict: The most affordable lockable station here, for 12 devices.
products.description:
The Learniture holds 12 devices with a one-point lock and cable grommet holes, in the $100 to $200 bucket, the lowest price tier in this ranking.

Eighth place is down to the fact that it holds the fewest devices and uses a single lock point. The lower price is the reward.

Buy it for a small group or office. Skip it if you need to secure more than 12 devices.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is the number of devices a cart holds. Pick one slightly larger than your set so you can grow. Check that the listing names the device types and sizes it fits, such as 14 inch laptops.
A lock on the front only leaves the back open on some carts. Front and rear locks secure both sides. Look for the words front and rear or back door locks in the bullets.
Casters let you move a cart between rooms, and locking ones stop it rolling while you load. Check for locking wheel wording.
Surge protection guards devices from power spikes during charging. Look for it by name in the listing.
A chain hook lets you tether the cart to a fixed object. It adds theft resistance in shared spaces, so check whether the listing mentions one.

howToChoose.subheading: Front and Rear Locks vs Single Lock

cards.label: Front and rear locks
cards.text: Secures both sides. The POCHAR 30 and Meteteel 20 list both.

cards.label: Single lock
cards.text: Simpler and cheaper. The Learniture 12 uses a one-point lock.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to front and rear locks.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Locks on both sides, supplied spare keys, and an anchor point.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The POCHAR 30 lists two keys per lock, and the POCHAR 20 lists a chain hook anchor point.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a full class set, where the POCHAR 30 provides 30 slots and two locks.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small group, where the Learniture 12 is in the lowest price tier.

faq.q: Can these carts hold both iPads and laptops?
faq.a: Several list iPads, Chromebooks, tablets and laptops. Check the maximum device size, such as 14 inches on the POCHAR 30.
It is better, because a front-only lock can leave the rear open. The POCHAR 30 and Meteteel 20 list both.

faq.q: Is a 30 device cart worth it over a 20 device one?
faq.a: Only if your set is larger than 20. Otherwise a smaller cart takes less room.

faq.q: How do I set up a cart?
faq.a: The Meteteel arrives fully assembled. Others may need assembly, so check each listing.

faq.q: How do I keep devices safe from power surges?
faq.a: The VEVOR lists surge protection. For others, check the listing or use a protected power source.

faq.q: What if I lose a key?
faq.a: The POCHAR 30 supplies two keys for each lock. Keep spares stored separately.

finalTake: The POCHAR 30 Unit is the best lockable cart for large classrooms, thanks to its front and rear locks. The Pearington 20 is the best mid-size choice because of its locking casters, and the Learniture 12 is the budget option. Match capacity to your device count first, then check the lock layout.
